claims.text: Ab-initio DFT cluster expansion can be used to tune the magnetic behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Compositional variations of ±5% can tune magnetic exchange interactions in non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Tuned magnetic exchange interactions shift magnetic phase transitions.
Shifts in magnetic phase transitions alter the magnetocaloric effect in low-dimensional configurations.
DFT cluster-expansion simulations over 300–800 K can model composition-dependent changes in structural order.
Small compositional variations induce changes in local atomic order.
Small compositional variations induce changes in chemical-disorder patterns.
Altered atomic configurations modify magnetic exchange interactions.
Changes in magnetic exchange interactions shift phase transitions governing the magnetocaloric response.
Composition tuning will produce a measurable shift in magnetic phase-transition temperatures relative to the baseline alloy.
Composition tuning will alter magnetocaloric entropy change relative to the baseline alloy.
Composition tuning will alter adiabatic temperature change relative to the baseline alloy.
The tuning effect may be limited when compositional changes exceed ±5%.
Surface or other low-dimensional effects omitted from the simulations may dominate the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior.
